blocks.content: The project list shows all customer projects, their assignees and how many client messages wait to be read or answered. Every project has its own page split into sub-pages (Overview, Conversations, Progress, Approvals, Updates, Access, Files, Settings). The client sees the project in the client portal and signs in with a personal account - a password, or a one-time code or link from an e-mail.

cards.title: Open a project
cards.text: The folder icon of a row opens the project page on the Overview sub-page (address web/projects/ID/overview). The pencil icon offers a quick edit in a dialog.

cards.title: Assignee
cards.text: The Assignee column shows the administrator responsible for the project. The My projects filter keeps only your projects. Only an active administrator who may edit projects can be the assignee.

cards.title: New messages and Waiting on us
cards.text: New messages = client messages nobody in the administration has read yet (filter Unread messages). Waiting on us = open threads where the client wrote last and waits for a reply.

cards.title: New project
cards.text: The form lets you pick a template - the project then gets its checkpoints with dates counted from today. After creating, the Access sub-page opens: the project has no user yet, and without one nobody can sign in to the portal.

cards.title: Project templates
cards.text: The Templates toolbar button opens the template management (web/projects/templates). A template has a name, description and a list of checkpoints, each with a title, description and an optional due date as days from the start (0-3650). Rows are added, moved with arrows and removed. Deleting a template does not change projects made from it.

blocks.content: The header shows the name, status, visibility, assignee and the number of unread messages, with the sub-page tabs below. Every sub-page has its own address (e.g. web/projects/7/conversations), so you can send it to a colleague or open it from an e-mail; switching tabs keeps unsaved settings. The Conversations tab shows the unread messages, the Approvals tab the requests waiting for the client.

cards.title: Overview
cards.text: Key numbers (waiting on us, approvals, progress, users, updates) - a click opens the sub-page - and what happened in the last 90 days: client messages, approval decisions, step changes, published updates. An item opens its place, a message the thread itself.

cards.title: Settings
cards.text: Name, assignee, lead, contacts, dates, visibility and status are edited in the form - a change shows the Save changes / Discard changes bar. Leaving with unsaved changes or an uncopied password asks first.

cards.title: Who gets team e-mails
cards.text: A client message goes to the thread assignee, otherwise the project assignee, otherwise the contact e-mail of the project. Client approval decisions are delivered the same way.

blocks.content: The Access sub-page holds the portal link (Copy link) and the list of client users. Every person on the client side has their own account: name (shown with their messages), login name (3-64 characters: lower-case letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore; unique in the project), an optional e-mail and the e-mail language (prefill only). The client cannot change the name, login name or password; in the portal they set only their e-mail and notifications.

steps.label: Add a user
steps.text: Fill in the name and login name and choose the access: with a password (typed in, at least 10 characters with letters and digits, or generated), send an invitation by e-mail, or both. An account without a password needs an e-mail and an invitation.

steps.label: Invitation
steps.text: An e-mail with a link that signs the client in with one click (valid 7 days, once). The envelope icon of an account sends it again any time - older links stop working.

steps.label: Handing over a password
steps.text: The password is shown only once. Copy sign-in details copies the link, login name and password at once. The password is never stored (only its hash).

steps.label: Forgotten password
steps.text: The client can sign in with a code from the e-mail. The key icon resets the password: a new one is generated, the old one stops working and the user is signed out everywhere.

steps.label: Removal
steps.text: The bin icon removes the user and signs them out. Their messages and decisions stay under their name.

cards.title: Sign-in with a code
cards.text: On the portal sign-in page the client picks Code by e-mail and enters the login name or e-mail. If the account has an e-mail, a six-digit code arrives (valid 15 minutes, 5 attempts, at most 5 codes an hour). The answer is always the same, so it does not reveal whether the account exists.

cards.title: Verified e-mail
cards.text: Using a code or a link verifies the e-mail of the account. When the e-mail changes, the verification is dropped and the notifications are switched off. An account shows the chips With password / No password, Invited and E-mail verified.

cards.title: E-mail notifications
cards.text: The client switches them on in the portal (My account), separately for: a reply in a thread, a step state change, a step date change, a new update and an approval request. Everything is off by default; the administration only shows the choice.

cards.title: What the e-mail contains
cards.text: Only the project name, the subject of the thread / step / update / request and a link to the portal - never the message text. The link opens the right part of the portal.

blocks.content: With the move to users, the former shared password of every project became a user with the login name klient (the password stayed the same). All existing sign-ins ended - the client signs in again with klient and their password. You can rename the user klient or create personal accounts instead.

Conversations show the threads of this project, split into Mine, Active, Closed and All. A thread with unread messages shows their number; opening it marks it read for the whole administration. An open thread shows Waiting on us or Waiting on the client and the thread assignee. The list refreshes itself every minute.

cards.title: Thread assignee
cards.text: In an open thread you pick the administrator responsible for it; they get an e-mail and from then on receive the client messages of the thread. The Mine filter shows the threads assigned to you.

cards.title: Reply to the client
cards.text: The message is signed with your name, the client sees it in the portal and users who switched on reply notifications get an e-mail.

cards.title: Internal note
cards.text: The Internal note switch above the message field: the note (with attachments) is seen only by the team, marked yellow, never shown to the client and does not change Waiting on us / on the client.

cards.title: Read by the client
cards.text: Your messages show Not read yet or Read by the client.

blocks.content: Checkpoints are the project steps the client sees in the portal under Progress. Each has a title, optional description, due date and an internal note the client never sees. The state is picked from a menu (Not started, In progress, Done); a state or date change e-mails the users who switched that on. Arrows change the order; an overdue step is marked.

cards.title: Apply a template
cards.text: Adds the checkpoints of a template after the existing ones; the dates are counted from the chosen start date.

cards.title: Save as a template
cards.text: Creates a new template from the checkpoints of the project (dates become days from the first date).

blocks.content: Use an approval request when you need a binding consent from the client - for a design, texts or the hand-over of a finished part. A request has a title, description, files, optionally a project step and the date by which the client should respond. Users with the notification switched on get an e-mail.

steps.label: Ask for approval
steps.text: The New request button. Until the client decides, the request can be changed (files too).

steps.label: The client decides
steps.text: In the portal they choose Approve, or Request changes with a required comment. The decision is saved with the account and time and cannot be changed; the assignee gets an e-mail.

steps.label: After changes
steps.text: For a request with Changes requested choose Ask again - the request goes back to the client, the history of decisions stays.

steps.label: Cancel and delete
steps.text: A cancelled request is hidden from the client. Only a request without a decision can be deleted; the others are a record.

blocks.content: Updates are news about the progress of the project (what is done, what is happening, what comes next), possibly with files. Write a draft and publish it later, or publish at once. The client sees only published updates; an e-mail is sent only at the first publication, not after an edit or publishing again. A published update can go back to a draft or be deleted.

The Files sub-page gathers the attachments of all threads, updates and approval requests, newest first, with size, date, author and a link to where they come from. Attachments of internal notes are marked Internal and hidden from the client, as are the files of draft updates and cancelled requests. Download links are time-limited.

sections.heading: 09. What the client sees in the portal

blocks.content: The client signs in through the project link - with a password, a code from the e-mail or the invitation link (a sign-in lasts 24 hours from the last activity). The portal looks like the administration: the user name, refresh and language at the top; on the left a menu with counts (news, approvals, unread messages, progress).

cards.title: Overview
cards.text: What is new since the last visit (new items highlighted), a notice of requests waiting for approval, progress in per cent, threads waiting for the client, the estimated date and the current step.

cards.title: Progress and Communication
cards.text: Checkpoints with dates and descriptions; threads with priority, Waiting on you / Supplier is replying and the authors of messages.

cards.title: Approvals and Updates
cards.text: Requests with description, files, step, deadline and the history of decisions, with Approve / Request changes; published updates with files.

cards.title: Files, Contacts, Help
cards.text: All public files with a link to their source, the project lead contact and the supplier's company details, the portal guide.

cards.title: My account
cards.text: Name and login name (read-only), the sign-in method and the e-mail verification, e-mail, e-mail language and five notification switches (all off by default, they cannot be switched on without an e-mail).

blocks.content: Without the web-projects-update permission the project page and the template management are read-only. The audit log records changes of the project, users (by id only), invitations and sign-ins by code / link (without the code and e-mail), checkpoints, thread assignment, approval requests with decisions (without the comment) and updates (without the text); messages, codes and passwords are never logged. Unused and expired sign-in codes are deleted automatically.
